brief.subject: Fake government passport helpers and a $106.8M debt relief ban
brief.headline: FTC Targets Government Impersonators in Passport and Debt Relief Schemes
brief.dek: A court shut down a debt relief scheme that preyed on seniors and veterans, and the FTC sued an alleged fake-government passport service.
brief.lede: Scammers posing as banks and government agencies are a top FTC target this week. A court entered a $106.8 million judgment against a debt relief operation aimed at seniors and veterans.

sections.heading: Debt Relief Scheme Permanently Shut Down
bullets: A federal court permanently banned operators of an alleged debt relief scheme, acting at the FTC's request.
The scheme targeted seniors and veterans, so older relatives and former service members are prime marks for this pitch.
Callers allegedly posed as banks, credit card companies and government agencies to seem trustworthy.
On October 14, 2026, the court entered a $106.8 million default judgment against the corporate defendants.

sections.heading: Passport Service Posed as the Government
bullets: The FTC sued GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman over an alleged government impersonation scheme.
The operation allegedly targeted people seeking passport services by claiming to be, or be tied to, the federal government.
Paid search ads were allegedly used to mimic the government, so a top search result is not proof of an official site.
The FTC also cites misleading promises and fake reviews, meaning glowing ratings can be manufactured.

sections.heading: FTC Reports to Congress on Older Adults
bullets: The FTC released Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026, its latest report to Congress on fraud against older adults.
It highlights trends drawn from fraud reports filed by older adults themselves.
The report also details enforcement actions against unfair or deceptive practices hitting older Americans.
